text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-Consumers do not want a free power market in Norway, according to a new poll from Opinion. People do not support a free market where the price of electricity is decided by supply and demand. Consumers also want a flat power price across the whole country.
-Two people were killed and three seriously injured in motorcycle accidents over the weekend. Traffic authorities have warned that autumn is the worse season for motorcycle accidents.

-Engineering and offshore group Kvaerner ASA wants to build a new bridge over Britain's River Thames. The company earns so much money in toll fees from a bridge at Dartford, south of London, that it wants to use future profits from the Dartford bridge to finance a new one in the area.
-Sales and prices of business properties have gone up this autumn, real estate agents say. One agent estimates sales volumes to be 20 to 30 percent higher than at the same time last year.
-The world's dry bulk fleet will be larger than the tanker fleet in the next few years, according to a new analysis by shipping brokers Fearnleys.
